The model authority sets (MAS) are defined for handling of boundary elements that occur at the regional network boundaries, wherein the globally unique reference IDs are allotted for unique identification of power system resources. The MAS approach supports easy merging of multiple regional CIM network models into a national CIM network model. The CIM profiles for network model exchange and state estimation applications are defined. Consequently, CIM/RDF/XML message payloads for the applications are generated for western region 400 kV network of Indian power grid.

articleTitle: Short circuit currents of DFIG based wind turbines
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 6th International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: The share of wind energy is growing day by day and asynchronous machines like doubly fed induction generators are finding their place in the grid. These asynchronous generators under transient conditions like fault behave in a different manner than synchronous ones. In order to achieve fault ride through capabilities for such generators special protection scheme is needed. One of the solution technique is to use crowbar resistances on rotor winding to protect the rotor side converter. During a fault, the current profile of DFIG is different compared to a conventional generator. This paper focuses on the short circuit current profiles of DFIG for wind turbines. An analytical expression is described for an asymmetrical fault current which is slip and initial condition dependent. Crowbar protection scheme and its effect on short circuit characteristics has been discussed. A brief analysis on the effects of these fault currents on generator circuit breaker is considered. Simulation results compared with theoretical analysis is presented for verification.

articleTitle: Application of DWT and ANN for fault classification and location in a series compensated transmission line
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 6th International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: In this paper an accurate approach is proposed for classifying and locating faults in series compensated (SC) network utilizing discrete wavelet transform (DWT) and artificial neural network (ANN). In the first phase of the proposed approach, fault current samples acquired from simulation were decomposed using Db5 mother wavelet. Faults signatures are captured in terms of standard deviation of detail coefficients of 1<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">st</sup> and 5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> level, norm entropy value of the wavelet coefficients and minimum and maximum value of the wavelet coefficients. In final phase, captured features are applied as input to classifier and distance estimator models for training and testing. For investigating the efficacy and accuracy of the proposed two-stage approach of classifying and locating faults in SC network, numerous test simulation have been carried out on a 400 KV, 300 km SC network in MATLAB environment. The results obtained from test cases, reveals that the proposed approach can reliably classify and locate the faults with high accuracy.

articleTitle: Bidding strategies of Gencos and large consumers in competitive electricity market based on TLBO
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 6th International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: In this paper, a new optimization technique known as Teaching Learning Based Optimization (TLBO) algorithm is proposed so that the Gencos and large consumers participating in bidding in the day ahead competitive electricity market can suitably bid so as to govern the MCP (Market Clearing Price) in their favour. Here other small consumers are present in aggregate form. The auction process continues until any participant is willing to change its bidding data with an objective to win the bid at any particular hour of the trading period. The results obtained implementing TLBO optimization method outperforms than that obtained using PSO when tested with IEEE-30bus system with 6 Generating Companies (Gencos) and 2 large consumers.

articleTitle: Real-time transient instability detection using frequency trend vector in wide area monitoring system
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 6th International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: Fast transient instability detection tools are required in stressed power system to avoid widespread power outages. In this paper, an instability detection method is developed for real-time application in the wide area monitoring system. The proposed method uses frequency measurements that are readily available from phasor measurement units. In order to subside the impact of rapid changes in the measurements on the instability detection, a frequency trend vector is considered. A stability index is introduced to evaluate the power system stability. Unlike stability prediction and forecasting, this paper focuses on present stability status of the system. The methodology proposed is demonstrated by using a 39 bus system.

articleTitle: Optimal location and sizing of STATCOM using Fuzzy-PSO approach
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 6th International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: In this paper, an evolutionary computing technique comprising of Fuzzy logic and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) Algorithm has been proposed for optimal location and sizing of STATCOM to improve the voltage stability and to minimize the total voltage deviation in a power system. The proposed Fuzzy-PSO Algorithm has been applied using two steps. As the first step, the weakest buses selected for placement of STATCOM using modal analysis. In the second step Fuzzy-PSO Algorithm has been applied for selecting optimal location of STATCOM considering these selected weakest buses. The proposed approach has been applied on the standard IEEE 30-bus system considering the most severe single line outage contingencies under normal loading and under stressed condition. The proposed Fuzzy-PSO approach has been found to be quite satisfactory.

articleTitle: Designing an optimized pitch controller of DFIG system using frequency response curve
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 6th International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: In last few years, a variable speed wind turbine employing a Doubly-Fed Induction Generator (DFIG) has turned into a standout amongst the most widely recognized wind energy conversion systems in view of its great efficiency, lessen mechanical stress on the turbine and comparatively small power rating of back-to-back converters, enhanced power quality and controllability, and so on. In this work, a control scheme has been used to regulate the real power, which based on the frequency response curve by utilizing a lookup table. The maximum power point tracking (MPPT) mechanism has likewise been contemplated in this paper to acquire the reference turbine speed for a given wind speed. The Hooke-Jeeves technique has been utilized to optimize the Proportional-Integral gain of pitch controller. The execution of the model and the proposed control procedure has been simulated by the MATLAB/ SIMULINK toolbox.

articleTitle: Ride-through capability improvement of a grid-integrated DFIG based wind turbine system using a new protection design
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 6th International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: Improvement of Fault-ride through (FRT) capability of grid integrated Doubly Fed Induction Generators (DFIGs) in wind energy system is an major issue of the power industry. In this paper a Novel Active Crowbar Protection (NACB_P) system is proposed and designed to enhance the Fault-ride through (FRT) capability of DFIG so as to improve the system stability. The importance of NACB_P is to maintain the connection of DFIG with the grid during fault condition to provide uninterruptable power supply to the loads. The major function of the capacitor used in the protection circuit is to eliminate the ripples generated in the rotor current and to protect the converter as well as the DC-link capacitor. The main objectives of the proposed approach are: minimisation of magnitude of rotor fault currents, maintaining constant DC-link voltage and the reactive power profile of the system. The proposed scheme is validated through a 1.7 MVA DFIG based WECS with different fault conditions in MATLAB/Simulation. An Experimental analysis is presented in this paper taking three phase grid fault into consideration.

articleTitle: Optimal capacitor placement in RDS using combined fuzzy & novel power loss sensitivity method
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 6th International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: This paper presents a new methodology for optimal capacitor placement problem in Radial Distribution System (RDS) in order to reduce the total power losses, to improve the voltage profile, to enhance voltage stability, and to achieve more energy savings. The main contribution of this paper is (i) fuzzy expert system (FES) is used to find the optimal locations for capacitor placement, (ii) A novel power loss sensitivity method is applied to determine the optimal capacitor size, (iii) Impact of capacitor placement on the system performance of the radial distribution systems is evaluated in terms of voltage profile, power losses, energy savings & voltage stability index (VSI), (iv) the annual cost of energy loss, total annual cost and net savings. The combined fuzzy & novel power loss sensitivity method is implemented on Existing rural 15 bus system and standard IEEE-34 bus distribution system, and the results are compared with an existing PSO method and Fuzzy-Harmony search algorithm (HSA).

articleTitle: A cross correlation control approach for multifunctional SPV system
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 6th International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: This work presents a two stage grid connected three-phase, four-wire (3P4W) SPV system using cross correlation control algorithm. This system not only feeds the power to the grid but it also helps in power factor correction and harmonics elimination. The proposed system includes the SPV string, a DC-DC boost converter, a voltage source converter (VSC), ripple filter and linear/nonlinear loads. For extracting maximum power from the PV string, a perturb and observe based MPPT algorithm is utilized. The fourth leg of the VSC is utilized for mitigation of neutral current at PCC in a 3P4W distribution network. A prototype of proposed system is realized in the laboratory and proposed control algorithm is experimentally verified on this developed system.

articleTitle: Effect on static and dynamic reactive power in high penetration wind power system with altering SVC location
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 6th International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: Wind generation is currently the leading form of new renewable generation in the world. The power generation through wind energy totally dependent on the flow of the wind due to uncertainty and randomness of wind flow, the generation of power is quite fluctuating in nature and large-scale wind farms may cause significant impact to the stability and power system safety. Wind power has significant variation over shorter time periods, but is growing very consistent from year to year. A significant amount of wind power is integrated into the power system day by day. With large variations in wind generation, reactive power flows on transmission lines and voltage are two major variables which affect the performance of the power system. The shunt connected FACT devices such as a static var compensator (SVC), which is dynamic reactive power compensator whose reactive power output depends upon the system voltage, is adopted for control of bus voltage magnitude and to bring the system near to unity power factor, thus for mitigation of reactive power. This paper presents the reactive power control by application of SVC in the power system having high wind power generation and its effect analyzed on static and dynamic var mitigation with the change of the location of SVC to far off the bus. For analysis Rajasthan Grid(India), comprising of different voltage level with high wind power penetration in the Western part selected. Mi.-Power software is used in actual field conditions simulation and analysis. The comparative effect of altering the location of SVC analyzed.

articleTitle: Comparative performance analysis of UPQC using two level and three level inverter for three phase three wire system
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 6th International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: As day by day increasing of technology, maintaining power quality becomes more essential for the industries and to the customers. The unified power quality conditioner can give the unique solution for all kind of power quality problems. This paper presents the comparative performance analysis of unified power quality conditioner using two and three level voltage source inverter topologies. For the three level diode clamped multilevel inverter has been selected. The simulation is implemented for both the systems in the MATLAB Simulink environment.

articleTitle: Improved Direct Torque Controlled IPM Synchronous Motor using variable band 12 sector control in two level inverter
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 6th International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: An improvement over the conventional 6-sector DTC (Direct Torque Control) is seen when the sectors are divided into 12, each being 30° in a 2-level inverter. The 12-sector approach is based on maximum utilization of available vectors as the 6-sector conventional control does not utilize all the vectors available. It is seen that the proposed 12-sector control minimizes the torque ripple in comparison to conventional DTC. IPM motor under DTC is used for analysis due to its rising importance. This paper establishes the 12-sector terminology, the switching table utilized and comparison of conventional 6-sector control to that of proposed 12-sector control. A 5 level torque hysteresis control is introduced to make use of the 12 sectors. The work also shows that having a variable inner hysteresis torque band improves the 12-sector with respect to different operating conditions i.e., speed and torque. The proposed control has been implemented and supported by simulation results.

articleTitle: Multi-function digital relay for power Autotransformer protection
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 6th International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: This paper introduces a multi-function digital relay to provide a complete protection for the three phase power autotransformers against different types of abnormalities. The conventional methods of differential protection have many drawbacks such as Current Transformer (CT) mismatch, vector group and CT saturation problems which cause a false operation for the relay. A typical ATP-EMTP model for 500/220 KV Autotransformer is presented in this paper to evaluate the suggested algorithm. The algorithm is based on calculating the negative sequence differential current, the phase difference between the primary and secondary currents and the fundamental frequency for the primary and secondary currents. The suggested technique satisfies high degree of reliability, security and dependability.

articleTitle: Distribution system planning and development for supporting economic — Social growth in Luangprabang province Lao PDR
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 6th International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: This paper, is a study on the planning and development of the electricity distribution system to supporting economic and society growth in Luangprabang, from the year 2015 -2025, and to reliability improvement of the electricity distribution system in Luangprabang branch, based on the rate economic and social growth. This study also the examined the rate of return on investment (economic rate of return, EIRR and benefit cost ratio, B/C ratio). Reliability is assessing of the system after improvement of the electrical distribution system. Evaluating reliability will be considered explicitly to provide power to ensure stability and power to shrink. Therefore, improvement it should be considered terms of avoiding costs. These avoid costs, related to the reliability of an electric system index: Energy Not Supply (ENS), System Average Interruption Frequency Index (SAIFI) and System Average Interruption Duration Index (SAIDI) [12].

Author Keywords: Distribution network system expansion and Economic justification

articleTitle: Indian experience of utilisation of Synchrophasor system and its integration with Situational Awareness system
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 6th International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: This paper describes utilization of Synchrophasor system by State Transmission Utility of Maharashtra in India and its experience in monitoring of the grid with the help of this. It discusses how synchrophasor system, Situational Awareness system can be utilized for Real time as well as Offline analysis of the grid in Indian context. It presents comparative analysis of occurrence in the grid with the help of Synchrophasor system, Disturbance Records of Numerical Relaying system and that of Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition System(SCADA). It also gives brief information on first of its kind of integration activity of WAMS and Situational Awareness System carried out in India further highlighting how it improved observability of the grid.

articleTitle: Fast Bus Transfer Systems - customized scheme requirements and implementation experiences
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 6th International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: After several decades of experiences, Fast Bus Transfer Systems are generally considered to be reasonably standardized in terms of their design, features, specifications, application and system integration. However, at a deeper level, there continue to be a wide variety of choices that OEMs, consultants, contractors and end-users need to make that have a significant impact on the operation philosophy, as well as the overall performance of the installation under various system conditions. This paper highlights some of the practical aspects of dealing with customized scheme requirements and the implementation experiences in various power plants and process industries.

articleTitle: Distribution system reconfiguration in a deregulated environment
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 6th International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: Amendment of vertically integrated electricity market into deregulated electricity market necessitates the consideration of locational marginal price (LMP) in economics of distribution system. Network reconfiguration for loss minimization may not be an economical operation of distribution system. This paper proposes network reconfiguration to minimize the cost of power purchased from the grid and that generated by the distributed generator in the distribution system. The proposed approach is applied to a 16-bus distribution system and the results are obtained.

articleTitle: Goal Attainment method for solving reactive power dispatch
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 6th International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: Reactive power dispatch is one of the primary tasks in the operation and control of a power system. This paper presents Goal Attainment method to solve the reactive power dispatch (RPD) problem. Reactive power dispatch is carried out to reduce real power losses, to improve the voltage profile and voltage stability in a power system. Goal Attainment method is a reliable optimization technique for obtaining near global optimization. For multi-objective optimization problems the Goal Attainment method is a powerful method to find the best compromising solution. To demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed Goal attainment based approach, it is implemented for reactive power dispatch in the standard IEEE 30-bus test system. The obtained results have been compared with the reported results using Genetic Algorithm based fuzzy goal programming, Differential Evolutionary technique and optimization Toolbox. On comparison, the Goal attainment based approach is found to be superior in terms of solution quality and speed.

articleTitle: Study on optimal harmonic energy harvesting from non-linear loads within enterprise buildings
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 6th International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: Increasing penetration of non-linear loads, results in lines carrying harmonic currents in addition to the fundamental frequency current. Harmonics cause increased losses in distribution system components and malfunctioning of certain sensitive loads. The problem is generally addressed by installing passive or active harmonic filters. However, rather than just suppressing them, if filter configurations are modified to harness energy associated with harmonics and utilize it for suitable applications, the cost of filter installation can be paid back. This paper proposes a concept of harvesting energy associated with dominant harmonic frequency component of sites having non-linear loads and utilize the energy for supplying heating loads present within the same premises. To harness the dominant harmonic energy, a tunable filter with harvesting load and a variable resistor is dynamically tuned to the harmonic frequency having dominant power at that instant. The paper also describes the possible filter configurations which can be utilized to harness the energy according to spectral components of the non-linear load present within the facility. Apart from harmonics, possibility of harvesting energy associated with other spectral components such as inter-harmonics and sub-harmonics is also discussed. To test the possibility of harvesting harmonic energy available in enterprise buildings a test site with predominantly computer/printer and HVAC load is considered and analyzed.

articleTitle: Deployment of Fuzzy based MRAS and IRFOC strategy with fast tracking for the sensorless speed control of SPIM
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 6th International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: The aim of this research paper is to provide a fast response and a high performance speed tracking trajectory of a sensorless speed control of single phase induction motor (SPIM) drive system at low, medium and high speeds using fuzzy logic controllers (FLCs). The fuzzy logic controllers (FLCs) are used in order to drive the rotor speeds and stator currents. The proposed method for the information of rotor speed is based on fuzzy logic-model reference adaptive system observer (FL-MRAS) strategy. Field-oriented control induction motor is adopted in order to obtain the high dynamic performance in the drive system. Simulation results proves to be fast tracking with quick settling time and steady response at low, medium, and high rotor speeds for a sensorless speed control of single phase induction motor drive system with fuzzy logic controllers (FLCs). The simulation of this paper is done by using Matlab/Simulink.

Author Keywords: Fuzzy Logic - Model Reference Adaptive System (FL-MRAS)

articleTitle: Design and analysis of LQR based controller for reactive power compensation
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 6th International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: This paper discusses a control design for compensating reactive power requirement in power distribution systems using Distribution Static Compensator (DSTATCOM). The DSTATCOM is realized using voltage source inverter and is controlled using PWM pulses generated through indirect current control. The current control utilizes optimal proportional controller gains designed using Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR) approach. The performance of the controller depends on the weighting matrix, which is chosen to ensure satisfactorily response. The DSTATCOM is controlled and designed using LQR based controller and Power Balance Theory (PBT) to generate the reference currents. The effectiveness of the control is verified through simulation results for the Matlab based model.

articleTitle: Cost effective d.c. distribution for remote area using hybrid energy (solar and biogas)
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 6th International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: In today's world the developing countries are looking for clean and cost effective energy solution for their sustainable development. The feasibility of using a hybrid energy combination of solar and biogas resource with d.c. distribution as a cost effective alternative solution for standalone areas where grid connection is practically not economical had been explored. The results are obtained using HOMER software and validates the proposal of d.c. distribution as an economical alternative solution for small remote areas.

articleTitle: Risk Constrained Short Term Hydro Scheduling using Two Point estimate method and conditional value at risk
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 6th International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: This paper presents application of Two Point estimate method to build a risk constrained model for generating optimal bids of hydro power plants in deregulated environment. Hydro Generation Company is considered as a price taker. Market prices are stochastic in nature and have been considered as exogenous variables. The objective is to find practically feasible hourly generation schedules/bids for operation of cascaded hydro plants of a medium size hydroelectric company (H-Genco) in day ahead manner. The challenge for H-GENCO is to consider the uncertainties involved in market price to maximize its profits. At same time all operational and technical constraints should be met, considering the risk involved due to market price variations. Two point estimate method (2PEM) has been used to accommodate the price uncertainty. This stochastic nature of input variable has been translated into the deterministic output results. Conditional value at risk (CVaR) is used as risk hedging tool and risk management constraints are added over the deterministic output results of 2PEM. Model takes into account all the possible operational, environmental and technical constraints related to machine and other details of generation units. Model is formed and solved as a MINLP optimization problem.

articleTitle: Improved cost analysis through smart grid network due to dynamic demand load response
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 6th International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: In developing electric smart grid network in general and demand respond in particular limits of a smart grid are a key factor affecting the efficiency of the overall grid system. Since conventional loading of grid system is often expensive, the estimation of smart grid power network rise by tools of mathematical modeling becomes increasingly important. Excepting for providing a more accurate representation of the problem, the proposed model can also reduce computing costs as well as time concern. This paper develops a minimal energy cost by bidirectional communication model algorithm using demand respond monthly data of West Bengal Power scenario and demonstrates its feasibility. This paper briefly summarizes the physical concept, calculation method and application possibilities of a selected time index that is described in greater detail in the references. Load models are also used when demand needs to adapt its hourly load level response to hourly electricity prices. Method of the examination was a comparison of the index values obtained by time domain numerical simulation realistic sample network. Objective of this paper is to develop proposed methods for demand respond for smart network development planning and to provide a possibility of real-time pricing monitoring for power system dispatcher use.

articleTitle: A low cost power quality management tool for different load types
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 6th International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: Any deviation of voltage or current from the ideal sinusoidal waveform is a power quality (PQ) disturbance. The economic loss caused by destruction of equipment due to poor quality i.e. leading or lagging VARs is significant and must be avoided. This paper shows the different kind of disturbances associated with linear and nonlinear loads. A low cost power quality monitoring system is developed by designing Virtual Instruments (VIs) using LabVIEW™ as a platform. With LabVIEW™ as development platform, real signals from chroma programming are used in LabVIEW algorithm by Data Acquisition (DAQ) card to acquire and digitize the input line signal to obtain the results. The results are obtained by simulating the VIs over different load conditions such as linear and nonlinear load. Further this paper also provide an approach which leads to fundamental idea regarding the reactive power control.

articleTitle: Model Predictive Control of multi functional inverter for grid tied photovoltaic generators
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 6th International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: With the increasing penetration of renewable energy sources and inclusion of additional features, the electrical networks have become more active. Every passing decade has seen newer features of the electrical network and with the emerging Smart Grid, distribution systems becomes active. Grid tied inverters are vital component of active distribution systems, acting as interfaces for the distributed generators. This paper presents Model Predictive Control (MPC) of a multifunctional inverter used for power quality compensation of non-linear local loads and grid integration of solar photovoltaic generators. By including the discrete nature of the switches in the power converter, the optimisation problem of MPC The reference current for the converter control is generated using Instantaneous Power theory. The control is simulated in MATLAB/ SIMULINK.

articleTitle: Time-variant slope compensation for peak current mode control (PCMC) of boost converter with point-of-load applications
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 6th International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: This paper describes the operation of a time-variant slope compensated peak current mode control (PCMC) for boost converter with POL configuration. The limitations of PCMC are minimized by introducing time-variant slope compensation and the effect of the RHP zero of boost converter is minimized by a type II compensator. The proposed work is evaluated and illustrated with wide range of line and load changes. Experimental results are presented for input range of 25V- 60V and load change of 0.6A - 2A with 400W power output at 10 kHz switching frequency. The transient response obtained is 25ms (250 cycles) for output voltage and the corresponding switch current stabilizes in 10ms (100 cycles) for 100% load changes respectively.

articleTitle: Real-time automatic generation control considering communication delays using linear matrix inequalities
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 6th International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: This paper investigates the effect of communication delays on dynamic performance of automatic generation control (AGC) of thermal power system. Field data of power system i.e. frequency and tie-line power deviations are transmitted over the dedicated data links to control centres of the plant. Sometimes these data links introduce communication delays in between and degrade the dynamic performance of the AGC system. These communication delays have not been considered in the existing models of AGC system. This paper, considers the effect of these communication delays and presents a realistic model for AGC system. The global controller has been designed for the centralized control scheme using linear matrix inequalities (LMIs) technique. The system has been studied in real-time environment, using three personal computers (PCs) connected in series named as real-time three PC system (RTTPS).

articleTitle: Conceptual analysis and representation of event-triggering mechanism in power system
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 6th International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: A conceptual design methodology is proposed for event-triggered based power system control. The event-triggering mechanism is adopted to reduce the communication burden between origin of the remote control signal and the controller location. The remote signal is transmitted to the controller location only when a pre-defined state dependent event-triggering condition, is satisfied. The triggering condition is derived from a stability criterion, and is monitored continuously by a separate event-monitoring unit located at the origin of the remote signal. The stability of the resulting closed loop system is guaranteed via the input-to-state stability (ISS) technique. The proposed event triggered mechanism is implemented on single machine infinite bus test power system. The validation of proposed mechanism is carried out through the simulation studies on MATLAB/Simulink platform. The numerical results show the efficacy of the controller in managing the communication channel usage without compromising the stated system stability objectives.

articleTitle: Measurement of steep impulse residual voltage on surge arrester blocks
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 6th International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: It's been decades since surge arresters became an integral part of power system. It protects the power system equipments by clamping the voltage to a safe level during the event of surge. The non linear characteristics of the metal oxide blocks used inside the arrester plays an important role in the operation of the arrester. The difference in the basic insulation level of the power system equipment and residual voltage of the arrester defines the protection margin of the system. The protection level of the arrester depends on the magnitude and steepness of the impulse current waveform, therefore the residual voltage across the arrester increases as time to crest reduces. Power system is subjected to fast transients caused due to bushing flashovers within valve hall, restrike of interrupting contacts, current chopping, etc. A higher residual voltage is observed when the arrester is subjected to a steep current surge, which in turn reduces the protection margin and in some cases even damaging the equipment. Steep impulse residual voltage consists of an inductive component that depends on the length of the arrester and a non-inductive component which is the property of the arrester block. This paper highlights the importance of estimating the non-inductive voltage drop across the arrester block as per relevant standards and computing protection level of the complete arrester when subjected to steep impulse current waveform in order to conduct proper insulation co-ordination study.

articleTitle: Harmonics and reactive current detection in a grid interfaced PV distribution system
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 6th International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: The abstraction of harmonic and reactive current component in a grid interconnected photovoltaic (PV) system is proposed in this work. The proposed approach is based on triangular function which is useful in signal processing and provides harmonics and reactive current detection to estimate reference current to control grid interconnected PV system. The proposed method is modeled and implemented in order to meet the grid requirements such as power quality (PQ) improvement, distortion free signals etc. The proposed technique for a three phase grid interconnected PV system is used to perform multi functions including, improved power quality, abstraction of maximum power from a given SPV array and feeding extracted solar PV power into the distribution system. Test as well as simulation results are vetted desirable performance of the proposed.

articleTitle: Power measurement using arduino for effective demand response
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 6th International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: The power demand has increased drastically over the last few years. One of the way by which we can solve this energy problems is by reducing usage of energy in households during peak demand. For this, demand response by real time pricing is implemented in the project. There is need for accurate and economic methods of power measurement. The main objective of this project is Power Measurement to reduce peak on generation by providing customers with their instantaneous power consumption. The aim of providing such data to the user is, to encourage them to shift their load during non-peak hour and reduce their power usage and electricity bill. Hardware, Software and the theory involved in the project is briefly described. The current and voltage signals from the load are stepped down and conditioned before they are given to the Atmega328. Load circuit, Signal conditioning circuit and their construction and functionality in the project are discussed.

articleTitle: A rational technique to maximize active power & diminish losses and reactive power of a DFIG
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 6th International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: In wind energy conversion systems (WECS), efficiency is of prime importance. For Doubly Fed Induction Generator (DFIG) based systems, to ensure maximum output, losses must be minimized. Reduction in reactive power may also facilitate an increased extraction of active power. This objective can be fulfilled by exercising proper control over direct axis rotor current (I<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">dr</sub>) and quadrature axis rotor current (I<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">qr</sub>). This work embodies a logical approach for determining the value of I<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">dr</sub> and I<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">qr</sub> which would yield maximum power from the DFIG. The aforementioned approach corresponds to a practical system because it concerns with minimization of reactive power. Most other works develop control schemes in which reactive power is considered zero. Simulation analysis using MATLAB 2010 has been done for validating the concepts mentioned in this paper.

articleTitle: Case study on analysis of bus bar protection relay tripping due to improper logic configuration
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 6th International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: -Modern numerical relays called as intelligent electronic device (IED), are embedded with advanced protection features to facilitate additional security features. Such security features eliminate the conventional topology of providing dual current transformers (CT) on either side of bus coupler circuit breaker (CB) to eliminate blind zones. Further, it also supports dynamic CT switching based on CB status, which assists elimination of blind spots, thereby eradicating the need for additional CT, thus providing a cost effective solution without compromise on protection. Such a solution implemented in a 220kV bus bar protection relay, encompassing double bus with transfer bus arrangement, located in Chindwara, Madhya Pradesh, has resulted in tripping of dual zones for a fault in a single zone, thus over riding the additional security logics. The analysis and precautionary measures carried out in this case, has been discussed in this paper to ensure that similar solutions can be adopted to inhibit analogous issues in future. This paper attempts to highlight the fact that the human errors may not be identified & eliminated during the installation, commissioning and testing phase at site. One has to remain vigilant throughout the product/ project lifecycle. This case is a live example of the same.

articleTitle: New Short Term Load Forecasting models based on growth rate scaling and simple averaging
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 6th International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: Load Forecasting is the link joining the strategic power system operation with the almighty mathematic algorithms in order to bring greater reliability, efficiency and economy in the system. This paper brings two novel forecasting engines, named SYGRSA and SYGRSAWP, for Short Term Load Forecasting (STLF), i.e., load forecasting with time leads ranging from one day to one week. STLF itself plays a crucial role in the control and scheduling operations of a power system. Modern techniques have been used to improve the accuracy of existing load prediction models using proper feature selection and consideration of necessary factors. The proposed models combine similar day approach, growth rate scaling and averaging techniques. SYGRSAWP is an optimised form of SYGRSA. Both the models have the potential to handle large historical data in short period of time. Moreover, they show remarkable forecasting accuracy. Further, a comparison between the two models has been analysed.

Author Keywords: Similar day Yearly Growth Rate Scaled Averaging (SYGRSA) Model
Similar day Yearly Growth Rate Scaled Averaging With Previous days (SYGRSAWP) Model

articleTitle: Novel method for steady state analysis of doubly-fed induction generator using MATLAB
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 6th International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: Wind energy outstands the renewable energy resources. The variable nature of wind energy is very well handled by doubly fed induction generators (DFIG). A deep and wide analysis of the steady state characteristics of DFIG under every possible condition is essential so that required power can be produced at any point of time by varying the independent variables. In this paper a detailed performance analysis of the DFIG is presented using MATLAB by varying all the three independent variables simultaneously and are shown with the help of three dimensional graphs.

articleTitle: Multi-input converter with regulated output voltage for series connected renewable energy systems
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 6th International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: A multi-input DC/DC converter with two renewable energy sources at input and one dc load at the output is proposed. The proposed converter draws power from two different sources. The converter maintains regulated output voltage even when one of the input sources diminish. The operation of the converter has been analyzed and the computer simulation results are obtained to validate the principle of operation of proposed multi-input converter.

articleTitle: Practical industrial applications of ultracapacitor technology in India - a case study
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 6th International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: Ultracapacitors have a unique positioning among various energy storage devices. Their features can be leveraged for a large number of industrial applications. This paper presents some of the innovation, design and system integration initiatives that have led to pioneering practical industrial applications of ultracapacitor technology in India in various domains such as Railways, Diesel Generators / Engines, Process Industries, Renewable Energy, Heavy Earth Moving Equipment etc. Use case scenarios which were tested, validated and finally adopted in real world conditions are presented with field data and analysis.

articleTitle: Large consumer's purchase portfolio optimization in electricity market
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 6th International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: Large consumers are increasingly involved in direct purchase from wholesale electricity markets, consisting of different markets and contractual instruments. Prices of these trading options are highly uncertain. Each trading options has it's own unique price-risk characteristic. Consumers may allocate their purchase among available trading options, to achieve minimum purchase cost while also minimizing risk. This work proposes a purchase portfolio optimization approach for large consumer's electricity procurement from spot market, multi-area bilateral contracts and self-generation, considering price uncertainties of pool and congestion charges, using Markowitz mean variance portfolio theory. Analysis based on a practical case of PJM market illustrates that due to interdependent behavior of multiple uncertain trading options, diversification potential of the portfolio is improved with multi-area trading. Results highlight that correlations between trading options strongly impact purchase allocation.

articleTitle: Network protection security enhancement based on power flow assessment
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 6th International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: Cascade tripping is a major reason for blackouts throughout the world. Events such as loss of large load or generation and faults may initiate undesirable relay operations, as a consequence of which the system may collapse. This paper proposes a method to identify distance relays in the system vulnerable to maloperate and determine preventive measures to avoid such a situation. Synchronized measurement from strategic locations in the network are obtained which are used for estimating the power flows in the system. Apparent impedance for relays at different buses in the system is calculated using active and reactive power flows of the connected lines. Two indices are introduced in this work: Relay Operation Proximity (ROP) and Security Margin (SM) which are calculated using apparent impedance. Index ROP is used to identify relays which are vulnerable to maloperate and SM provides change in power flow required to avoid relay maloperation. The proposed method is verified for the 39-bus New England system using PSCAD/EMTDC simulations.

articleTitle: Performance analysis of Open UPQC using three level diode clamped multilevel inverter
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 6th International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: Nowadays power quality has become the most important issue for the industrial and high end customers because of increasing the power quality problems with wide range use of nonlinear loads. The unified power quality conditioner can provides the overall solution for all type of power quality problems. But the recent development of Open UPQC structure can provide the optional use of installing the power converters for the different kind of customers depending upon the severity of power quality issue. This paper presents the implementation of Open UPQC structure with three level diode clamped multilevel inverter for three phase three wire system. The model is implemented in the MATLAB Simulink environment.

articleTitle: Hilbert space analysis for power networks
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 6th International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: Phasor methods of analysis for ac networks are well documented. Analysis proposed in this paper works with only scalars. Hilbert spaces are shown to constitute power description of generators and circuit elements and admit efficient computational analysis for power distribution. Circuit elements are characterized by Hilbert spaces which are fractions of larger Hilbert spaces of generators. Inner products of Hilbert spaces in elements afford convenient meaning of physical power. The analysis lends itself to interesting geometric interpretation of electrical variables. New results for power distribution are derived. Computational procedures based on this analysis are expected to be useful especially in power systems.

articleTitle: Multiple PMSG fed Non-inverting buck-boost converter for HEVs
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 6th International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: Presently, the Hybrid Electric Vehicle(HEV) industry is driven by the battery technology and its power management. For charging the batteries there is requirement of Permanent magnet synchronous generator (PMSG) and power converters. The authors in this paper are exploring the prospects of multiple/dual stator PMSG instead of single PMSG. The interconnection of multiple PMSGs using Matrix of switches create several voltage levels, enhancing the charging range of the batteries under variable speed operation of the vehicle. In particular, at low speed the charging of the battery depends on the size of the inductor of the Buck-boost converter. The interconnection permits the PMSGs to operate near rated full load, preserving the energy efficiency of the drive. In this work, the dc output voltage is regulated using Non-inverting buck-boost converter at 160V under 48–180V AC(around 70–240 volt DC) input voltage variation of the PMSGs, reducing the size and cost of the Power converter.

articleTitle: A synchro-phasor based wide area protection scheme for interconnected power grids
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 6th International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: More recent development in smart grid technology and communication system, power protection of transmission system leads to next level of digitization. The proposed technique shows the feature with digital protection of system integration protection scheme (SPIS) for large power transmission grids to address faults based on phasor measurement units. The fundamental assumption of the protection scheme depends on comparing positive sequence voltage magnitudes at each bus during fault conditions inside a local backup protection centre to locate the nearest bus to the fault. Then the absolute differences of positive sequence current angles are compared for all lines connecting to this bus to detect the faulted line. This new technique depends on synchronized phasor measuring technology with high speed communication system synchronized with GPS clock pulse. The simulation of the interconnecting system is applied on 220 kV Odisha Power Transmission Corporation (OPTCL) network using Matlab Simulink. The new technique can successfully distinguish the faults for interconnected lines. The new protection scheme works as unit protection system for long transmission lines.

articleTitle: Diagnosis of rotor winding shorts through signal reflection
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 6th International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: Inter turn shorts are of major concern in rotor windings of high speed turbine generators (TG) which result in excess vibration, over excitation energy and higher temperature. Recurrent Surge Oscilloscope (RSO), a condition assessment test tool is getting popular in Indian power industry for shorted turns identification and localization in field windings. This paper objective is to detect inter turn short circuits in TG rotor windings by recurrent surge oscilloscope (RSO) which works on time domain reflectometry (TDR) principle. Rotor winding is modeled as equivalent electric circuit of transmission line with cascade sections of RLC network for electric and magnetic field transfer. A delay line unit is constructed to get hands-on experience of RSO method and to understand the resultant signal reflection waveforms. Test data of RSO on 30MW, 11KV TG faulty rotor is presented before and after fault rectification. Some more experiments have been conducted by deliberate shorts creation and interpretation of the reflection signals are discussed. This study shows that RSO is a sure shot test in detection of inter turn shorts over the traditional approaches for right refurbishment action.

articleTitle: Single switched inductor capacitor coupled transformerless high gain converter for PV application
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 6th International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: This paper presents a new single switched inductor-capacitor coupled transformer-less high gain DC-DC converter which when directly fed from PV in which the low dc output voltage of PV module is converted into high dc output voltage. A state space model of the proposed converter is also presented in the paper. The constant output voltage of 300V is obtained by close loop control of converter using PID controller for different input voltage from PV module. PID controller is designed using Ziegler Nichols Method. Thirty six solar cells are used to design a PV module connected to the dc-dc converter. A MPPT controller using Perturb and Observe algorithm is used to find the maximum power point of the PV module. All the simulations are done in MATLAB-SIMULINK environment.
